# **Benchmarks, Architectural Trade-Offs, and Diagnostic Ablation Frameworks for Singer Identification on Artist20**

Automatic singer identification (SID) from polyphonic audio recordings is a complex task within Music Information Retrieval (MIR). Unlike general speaker recognition or audio tag classification, SID systems must isolate the subtle, pitch-varying timbral characteristics of the human vocal tract while disregarding background instrumentation, harmonic accompaniment, and recording studio production effects1. The Artist20 dataset, introduced by Ellis, is a benchmark for evaluating automated singer identification models1. Comprising 1,413 full-length MP3 tracks across 20 distinct pop and rock artists, the dataset assigns exactly six albums to each artist3.  
A central challenge in evaluating models on Artist20 is the "producer effect," or album-level confounding factor5. When models are evaluated using random track-level or frame-level splits, deep architectures often learn to recognize the specific production signatures, equalizations, and instrumental arrangements of individual albums rather than the vocal timbre of the singer2. Models evaluated under random splits can achieve deceptively high accuracy (exceeding 93% F1 score)6, but often fail to generalize when presented with the same singer performing in a different album setting5. To measure genuine vocal generalization, Hsieh et al. established a strict evaluation protocol using an album-level split, where four albums per artist are assigned to training, one album to validation, and one album to a held-out test set1.  
This report presents a state-of-the-art (SOTA) comparative leaderboard for Artist20 under the official album-level split protocol. It also provides an analysis of recent transfer learning results using speaker verification embeddings and outlines a suite of diagnostic ablation frameworks for experimental validation.

## **State-of-the-Art Leaderboard and Comparative Analysis on Artist20**

Published systems on Artist20 evaluated under the album-level split can be categorized by their input audio representations (raw polyphonic mixtures versus separated vocal signals) and modeling paradigms (fully supervised models trained from scratch versus transfer learning via pretrained self-supervised or speaker verification embeddings).

### **Published SOTA Performance Summary**

Historical approaches on Artist20 have evolved from classical hand-crafted timbral feature extraction to end-to-end Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks (CRNNs), non-local attention architectures, and multi-stream hybrid feature fusion models1. The table below summarizes the published systems evaluated under the album-level split constraint.

| Model / System | Modality & Separation | Pretraining / Feature Fusion | Target Metric | Reported Performance | Source / Reference |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **SVM Baseline** | Raw Mixture (MFCCs) | None (Hand-crafted) | Test F1 (Avg) | 0.48 \- 0.49 | Hsieh et al., 20202 |
| **Baseline CRNN** | Raw Mixture (Mel-Spec) | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Avg) | 0.603 \- 0.670 | Nasrullah & Zhao, 2019; Hsieh et al., 20202 |
| **Baseline CRNN** | Vocal-Only (Open-Unmix) | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Avg) | 0.610 | Hsieh et al., 20205 |
| **CRNN \+ Data Augmentation** | Shuffle-and-Remix | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Avg) | 0.740 | Hsieh et al., 20205 |
| **CRNNM \+ Data Augmentation** | Polyphonic \+ CREPE Melody | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Best) | 0.750 | Hsieh et al., 20202 |
| **CRNN FGNL (Full)** | Raw Mixture | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Best) | 0.800 | Zhang et al., 2021 (AAAI)1 |
| **CRNN FGNL (Full)** | Vocal-Only (Open-Unmix) | Trained from scratch | Song F1 (Best) | 0.830 | Zhang et al., 2021 (AAAI)1 |
| **Attention-CRNN-KNN (KNN-Net)** | Raw Mixture | Deep Timbre Representation | Song Accuracy | 0.850 (F1: \~0.83) | Sun et al., 20217 |
| **CRNN \+ X-Vector \+ Middle-Level** | Raw Mixture | Inception-V3 (L4) \+ X-vector | Song F1 (Best) | **0.860** (Avg: 0.810) | Zhang et al., 20222 |

### **Architectural Evolution and Metric Distinctions**

A detailed examination of published literature reveals key distinctions across evaluation metrics (F1 score versus Top-1 Accuracy) and temporal aggregation methodologies (segment/frame-level predictions versus whole-song majority voting)1:

* **From-Scratch Polyphonic Baselines**: Early deep learning architectures, such as the CRNN introduced by Nasrullah & Zhao, employ a stack of four 2D convolutional layers, two Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers, and a dense output layer5. Evaluated on raw polyphonic audio under the album split, this baseline achieves a frame-level F1 score of approximately 0.50 and a whole-song F1 score between 0.603 and 0.6702.  
* **Vocal Source Separation & Augmentation**: Hsieh et al. demonstrated that passing isolated vocal stems directly into a standard CRNN yields a lower song-level F1 score (0.610) than using raw polyphonic mixtures (0.670), primarily due to source separation phase artifacts and missing harmonic context5. However, when separated vocal tracks were artificially shuffled and remixed with background instrumentals from other tracks ("shuffle-and-remix" data augmentation), the album confounding factor was mitigated, raising the song-level F1 score to 0.7405. Integrating explicit pitch representations via a CREPE melody contour branch (CRNNM) pushed the song-level F1 score to 0.7502.  
* **Non-Local Context & Attentive Aggregation**: The Fully Generalized Non-Local Network (FGNL) proposed by Zhang et al. extends non-local operations across spatial positions, feature channels, and network layers while applying Gaussian smoothing filters to suppress feature map noise1. FGNL achieved a song-level F1 score of 0.800 on raw audio mixtures and 0.830 on vocal-separated audio, representing the highest performance published for an end-to-end network trained strictly from scratch without external pretraining data1.  
* **Hybrid Pretrained Speaker and Timbral Features**: The highest published benchmark on Artist20 under the album split is achieved by Zhang et al. (2022)2. Their architecture combines frame-level spectrogram features, middle-level perceptual music features extracted from an intermediate layer (L4) of a deep vision network (Inception-V3 trained on music classification), and timbral speaker embeddings (X-vectors) derived from speaker recognition models2. This multi-stream hybrid architecture achieved a peak testing F1 score of **0.860** (with an average F1 score across trials of 0.810)2.

### **Forensic Analysis of the Frozen ECAPA-TDNN Evaluation**

The pipeline evaluated in your experiments achieves a Top-1 accuracy of **95.2%** (Top-3 accuracy of 98.7%) using a frozen ECAPA-TDNN encoder (speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb) paired with a 2-layer MLP classifier probe trained on raw audio mixtures.  
Comparing this result against the published leaderboard shows that 95.2% accuracy is substantially higher than the best published from-scratch SOTA (FGNL at 83.0% F1)1 and exceeds the hybrid X-vector model (86.0% F1) by nearly 10 percentage points2. While speaker verification embeddings are inherently suited for singer identification, an accuracy of 95.2% on raw polyphonic mixtures warrants verification against specific evaluation pitfalls.

#### **Hypotheses Explaining Performance Superiority**

The performance of ECAPA-TDNN (Emphasized Channel Attention, Propagation and Aggregation in TDNN) stems from its pretraining objective on VoxCeleb—a dataset containing over one million speech utterances recorded across diverse acoustic environments, background noises, and transmission channels. The network's loss function (Additive Angular Margin Softmax) forces it to map vocal tract resonances, pitch-independent formants, and glottal source characteristics onto a compact, hyperspherical embedding space while suppressing non-vocal background noise. When applied to music, ECAPA-TDNN treats background instrumentation as additive ambient noise, isolating the singer's vocal timbre without requiring explicit source separation software.  
Conversely, general music self-supervised learning (SSL) models like MERT-v1-95M are pretrained using masked language modeling over Constant-Q Transform (CQT) and acoustic token targets. These targets incentivize the representation of polyphonic harmony, key, instrumentation, and rhythm—the exact confounding factors that lead to album-level overfitting on Artist205.

#### **Methodological Checks and Evaluation Pitfalls**

To verify that the 95.2% Top-1 accuracy reflects genuine generalization rather than an evaluation artifact, four methodological checks should be conducted:

> 1. **Album-Level versus Song/Chunk-Level Partition Leakage**: Confirm that the validation set partition contains no audio chunks or songs from albums present in the training set. If the split was performed randomly at the track or 5-second chunk level, the ECAPA-TDNN probe will memorize album production signatures, resulting in scores above 95%6.  
> 2. **Temporal Overlap and Frame-Level Leakage**: If embeddings were extracted from overlapping sliding windows (for example, 5-second windows with a 2.5-second hop) prior to splitting into train and validation sets, adjacent overlapping frames from the same song would appear in both partitions. Audio feature vectors must be extracted and partitioned strictly at whole-song or whole-album boundaries prior to chunking.  
> 3. **Validation Set versus Held-Out Test Set Evaluation**: The reported 95.2% metric reflects performance on the validation set. In small datasets like Artist20 (where one album per artist represents roughly 15 to 20 tracks per class in validation), hyperparameter tuning or early stopping on the validation set can introduce variance. Performance must be confirmed on an untouched, held-out test album set across multiple random album-split seeds2.  
> 4. **Vocal Activity Masking versus Silent Segment Pooling**: Polyphonic tracks contain instrumental intro, outro, and bridge sections where no singing voice is present. If temporal mean-pooling is applied across an entire raw track, the ECAPA-TDNN model encodes background instrumental audio. If the MLP probe classifies these instrumental embeddings accurately, the model may be identifying the artist by the instrumental signature (album confound) rather than the vocal timbre.

## **Per-Method Ablation Protocols and Diagnostic Frameworks**

To convert empirical measurements into actionable insights, the following diagnostic frameworks provide detailed protocols for explaining model behaviors across the baseline suite.

### **Classical Machine Learning: Feature Group Attribution and RF Importance**

The classical machine learning baseline using Support Vector Machines with a Radial Basis Function kernel (SVM-RBF) achieved 59.3% Top-1 accuracy, outperforming several deep learning architectures trained from scratch (such as FGNL at 57.1% and the Tagging CRNN at 58.4%). Analyzing why hand-crafted timbral features perform strongly provides insight into the feature space necessary for SID.  
Audio feature extraction pipelines in classical MIR typically process 16kHz mono audio by extracting frame-level acoustic descriptors, including MFCCs, Chroma, Spectral Contrast, Spectral Centroid, Bandwidth, Rolloff, Zero Crossing Rate, and Tonnetz features. These descriptors are summarized using mean and standard deviation pooling per track, normalized via a StandardScaler, and passed to a downstream classifier such as SVM-RBF or RandomForest.

#### **Per-Feature-Group Ablation Framework**

The input representation comprises several feature families concatenated into a track-level vector. To isolate the predictive power of each group, systematically evaluate the system under single-group removal (leave-one-group-out) and single-group isolation settings.

| Feature Group | Component Features | Dimensionality (Mean \+ Std) | Diagnostic Hypothesis |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Timbre** | MFCCs (13-20), ![][image1], ![][image2] | ![][image3] | Primary driver of vocal tract geometry; high performance indicates strong reliance on timbral formants. |
| **Spectral Shape** | Centroid, Bandwidth, Rolloff, ZCR | ![][image4] | Captures brightness and energy distribution; vulnerable to mastering and album production EQ. |
| **Harmonic/Tonal** | Chroma STFT, Tonnetz | ![][image5] | Captures musical key and chord progressions; acts as a direct proxy for album/genre confounds. |
| **Sub-band Energy** | Spectral Contrast | ![][image6] | Measures peak-to-valley ratios; balances instrumental density and vocal prominence. |

#### **Random Forest Feature Importance Analysis**

To complement the SVM ablation, leverage the Random Forest model (55.0% Top-1) to compute two distinct feature importance metrics:

> 1. **Mean Decrease in Impurity (MDI)**: Quantifies the total Gini impurity reduction brought by each feature across all trees. Features capturing album-specific keys (Chroma and Tonnetz) often exhibit artificially inflated MDI because they provide clean early splits on training albums.  
> 2. **Permutation Feature Importance (PFI) on Validation Set**: Evaluates the drop in validation accuracy when a specific feature column is randomly shuffled. Features with high MDI but low validation PFI indicate overfitted album-confound features, whereas features with high validation PFI represent robust, generalizable singer descriptors.

### **From-Scratch CRNN Architecture Family: Data Bottlenecks and Ensemble Diversity**

The deep models trained from scratch—including CRNN2D\_elu2 (64.9%), Nasrullah & Zhao CRNN (61.9%), minzwon CRNN (58.4%), and FGNL (57.1%)—cluster within a 57% to 67% Top-1 accuracy band despite architectural differences in parameter counts and attention mechanisms1.

#### **Learning-Curve Subsampling Ablation**

To test whether these models are fundamentally constrained by dataset scale (\~950 training tracks) rather than network capacity, construct a learning-curve ablation. Train each model on fractional subsets of the training set: ![][image7], ensuring that album-level partitioning constraints are strictly maintained.  
Analyzing the relationship between training loss and validation error across these subsets reveals the underlying bottleneck regime:

* **Data-Bottlenecked Regime**: Characterized by a large generalization gap where validation error plateaus early while training error approaches zero. If validation accuracy scales log-linearly with training set size without saturating, the architectures are data-starved.  
* **Capacity/Representation Bottlenecked Regime**: Characterized by a narrow generalization gap where training and validation errors converge at a relatively high loss value. If validation performance plateaus at 50% data volume and training loss cannot be further minimized, the models lack the inductive bias necessary to isolate vocal features from polyphonic mixtures.

#### **Model Disagreement and Ensemble Diversity Metrics**

To assess whether architectural differences cause models to make distinct errors or fail on the same difficult tracks, compute pairwise diversity metrics across the validation set predictions:

> 1. **Cohen’s Kappa Coefficient (![][image8])**: Measures inter-model agreement adjusted for chance agreement:  
>    ![][image9]  
>    where ![][image10] is the observed proportional agreement between Model ![][image11] and Model ![][image12], and ![][image13] is the expected chance agreement. Low ![][image8] values (![][image14]) indicate high architectural diversity.  
> 2. **Disagreement Measure (![][image15])**: The ratio of tracks where model ![][image16] and model ![][image17] make different predictions:  
>    ![][image18]  
> 3. **Oracle Ensemble Upper Bound**: Compute the accuracy of an "Oracle" selector that marks a prediction correct if *any* model in the CRNN pool correctly predicts the artist. If the single best model achieves 64.9% but the Oracle Ensemble achieves \>82%, ensembling via soft-voting or stacking will yield performance gains.

### **Representation Probing: MERT (Music-SSL) versus ECAPA-TDNN (Speaker Verification)**

The experimental gap between frozen MERT-v1-95M (68.4%) and frozen ECAPA-TDNN (95.2%) highlights a divergence between general music self-supervised learning and domain-specific speaker verification representations8.  
In processing raw audio mixtures, MERT-v1-95M extracts polyphonic and harmonic tokens that are subsequently mapped to an MLP probe, achieving 68.4% Top-1 accuracy. In contrast, ECAPA-TDNN isolates vocal tract timbre formants, feeding into the same MLP probe architecture to reach 95.2% Top-1 accuracy.

#### **Classifier Head Intermodality Swaps**

To confirm whether this performance gap originates from the intrinsic quality of the feature space or the interaction between embedding dimensionality and classifier head complexity, evaluate both frozen embeddings across three probe architectures:

* **Linear Probe**: Computes logits via ![][image19], evaluating whether artist identity is linearly separable in the unprojected embedding space.  
* **2-Layer MLP Probe**: Computes logits via ![][image20], testing whether non-linear projections are required to disentangle artist clusters.  
* **Cosine / Prototype Classifier**: Computes class centroids ![][image21] and predicts via ![][image22], measuring intra-class compactness without trainable parameters.

#### **Geometric Embedding-Space Topology Diagnostics**

Directly evaluate the geometric properties of the saved validation set embeddings ![][image23] extracted from MERT and ECAPA-TDNN without further model training:

> 1. **Mean Silhouette Coefficient (![][image24])**: Quantifies cluster cohesion versus separation:  
>    ![][image25]  
>    where ![][image26] is the mean intra-class distance of sample ![][image11], and ![][image27] is the mean distance to the nearest neighboring class cluster. A higher ![][image24] score for ECAPA-TDNN confirms tighter artist clusters.  
> 2. **Fisher Discriminant Ratio (FDR)**: Measures the ratio of between-class variance to within-class variance across feature dimensions:  
>    ![][image28]  
> 3. **Linear SVM Probe Proximity**: Train a linear C-SVM on both representations. The resulting margin width and support vector density directly indicate whether MERT's performance lower bound stems from non-linearly entangled polyphonic features.

### **Vocal Source Separation Granular Error Attribution**

In the CRNN2D\_elu2 experiments, applying Demucs source separation to extract vocals yielded a performance increase of \+2.2 percentage points (64.9% raw mixture to 67.1% vocals-only). Granular error attribution clarifies whether source separation provides marginal global improvements or targets specific acoustic arrangements.

#### **Per-Artist Class-Wise Gain Analysis**

Compute the per-artist accuracy delta:  
![][image29]  
Correlate ![][image30] with the acoustic density and arrangement style of each artist:

* **Positive Gain Artists (![][image31])**: Typically feature heavy arrangement density, distorted guitars, or dense brass sections where accompaniment masks vocal formants.  
* **Negative Gain Artists (![][image32])**: Typically feature sparse acoustic arrangements (such as acoustic singer-songwriters) where Demucs separation artifacts introduce phase distortion without providing noise-reduction benefits.

If ![][image38] and ![][image36] are both large, vocal separation alters the feature manifold—fixing specific tracks while degrading others—even though the net accuracy shift (+2.2pp) appears small.

### **Zero-Shot Audio-LLM Optimization: Non-Gradient Strategies for Qwen2-Audio**

Zero-shot evaluation of Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct achieved 47.5% Top-1 accuracy on a 40-track subset using basic prompting10. Audio Large Language Models (Audio-LLMs) can be optimized further without gradient-based fine-tuning using inference-time techniques10.

#### **Structured Prompt Engineering and Constrained Decoding**

Generic text prompts often allow the LLM to generate descriptive prose or hedge its predictions, leading to parsing errors. System prompts should establish a clear role, such as a master musicologist specializing in singer identification, and provide a strict closed candidate list of the 20 target artists. Instructing the model to output a structured JSON object containing the exact candidate name and confidence score standardizes parsing.

* **Constrained Logit Decoding**: Rather than generating open-ended text, restrict the model's output vocabulary during autoregressive generation. Force the LLM decoder to evaluate only the token sequences corresponding to the 20 candidate artist names, computing the softmax probability directly over those exact token IDs.

#### **Audio In-Context Learning (ICL) with Reference Exemplars**

Qwen2-Audio supports multi-turn interleaved audio-text inputs10. Construct an In-Context Learning (ICL) prompt by embedding short (3–5 second) isolated vocal exemplars of candidate artists directly within the prompt context11. Providing reference audio clips for candidate artists alongside a query audio clip allows the model to compare vocal characteristics directly, grounding its textual knowledge in raw acoustic properties and improving zero-shot discrimination11.

#### **Self-Consistency and Temperature Sampling Ensemble**

To improve decoding stability on noisy polyphonic inputs:

> 1. Sample ![][image41] to ![][image42] independent inference paths from Qwen2-Audio by setting the generation temperature ![][image43] and enabling top\-![][image44] (nucleus) sampling14.  
> 2. Extract candidate predictions across all paths and apply a majority-voting consensus scheme:  
>    ![][image45]  
> 3. Alternatively, average the predicted log-probabilities of the target candidate tokens across all sampled paths to yield a calibrated prediction.

## **Actionable Experimental Recommendations**

Evaluating the Artist20 dataset under an album-level split requires addressing the confound between instrumental production signatures and vocal timbre2. The analytical frameworks detailed above lead to four structured steps for pipeline optimization and reporting:

> 1. **Verify Split Protocols**: Prior to finalizing the 95.2% ECAPA-TDNN baseline result, perform an audit of the dataset split. Confirm that no tracks from validation albums appear in the training set and that feature pooling is restricted strictly to non-silent vocal segments.  
> 2. **Standardize Evaluation Metrics**: Report both song-level majority-voted Top-1 accuracy and song-level F1 scores across three independent album-split random seeds to ensure direct comparability with published literature2.  
> 3. **Isolate Embedding Topologies**: Implement the proposed linear and prototype probe swaps on ECAPA-TDNN and MERT embeddings. Computing the Silhouette Coefficient and Fisher Discriminant Ratio will confirm whether speaker verification pretraining successfully removes polyphonic background noise2.  
> 4. **Characterize Source Separation Shifts**: Apply McNemar's test and per-artist accuracy delta calculations to the Demucs vocal separation results. This distinguishes whether source separation provides a uniform shift or alters performance on dense acoustic arrangements5.
